# TemporaryFile

A temporary file that owns both its contents and its name.

```rux
pub struct TemporaryFile {
    pub file: File;
    // private fields
}
```

Move-only. [`Close`](/docs/api/filesystem/temporary-file#close) deletes the file and reports what the deletion said; destruction does the same with the outcome
discarded. [`Keep`](/docs/api/filesystem/temporary-file#keep) gives up ownership of the name instead, for the caller who has decided the file should
outlive this value — which is what a rename into place is built on.

| Name   | Type   | Description    |

| `file` | `File` | The open file. |

## Associated functions

<h3 id="create"><code>Create</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Create(allocator: Allocator, directory: Path, prefix: char8[..]) -> TemporaryFile ! IoError
```

Creates a new temporary file in `directory`, named from `prefix` and sixteen hex digits of entropy.
The file is opened for reading and writing and is created, never opened: a name that already exists is a
collision, and the next name is tried.

| Name        | Type        | Description                             |
| ----------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `allocator` | `Allocator` | where the storage comes from            |
| `directory` | `Path`      | the directory to create it in           |
| `prefix`    | `char8[..]` | the text the generated name starts with |

**Returns**: the created file, which is removed when closed unless kept

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Temporary.rux#L105)

## Destructor

```rux
func ~TemporaryFile(self: &var TemporaryFile)
```

Closes and deletes with the outcome discarded: the safety net, not the contract.
A destructor has nowhere to report a failed deletion, so a caller who needs to know calls [`Close`](/docs/api/filesystem/temporary-file#close). What
this guarantees is that a temporary file is never left behind by an early return or a failure path, which
is the reason the type exists.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Temporary.rux#L169)

## Related

<h3 id="temporary-name-attempts"><code>TemporaryNameAttempts</code></h3>

```rux
pub const TemporaryNameAttempts: uint = 4;
```

How many names are tried before a temporary file gives up.
With 128 bits of name, one collision is already a surprise and three in a row is not chance; failing is the
honest response to an entropy source that has stopped being one.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Temporary.rux#L26)

<h3 id="temporary-directory"><code>TemporaryDirectory</code></h3>

```rux
pub func TemporaryDirectory(allocator: Allocator) -> PathBuffer ! IoError
```

The directory the system sets aside for temporary files.
On Windows this is what the platform reports, which consults `TMP`, `TEMP` and `USERPROFILE` in turn. On the
Unix systems it is `/tmp`: reading `TMPDIR` needs environment access this package does not have yet, so a
caller who must honor it passes the directory to the functions below instead.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Temporary.rux#L35)

**Returns**: the system's directory for temporary files
